meta.subject: Verify agent-harness repos and terminology
meta.scope: Read-only primary-source verification of candidate agent harnesses and user terminology. No production code modified.
method: GitHub REST API for repository metadata, releases, tags, commits, root trees, README and LICENSE (E1).
Raw repository files at default branch (README, package.json, pyproject.toml, setup.py, server.json, CHANGELOG.md, selected source files) for stated claims (E2).
Official paper and product websites fetched directly (E3).
GitHub repository search API and general web search only for terminology discovery; every hit re-verified against its own record (E4 leads).
source_hierarchy: E2 repository source file at main
E3 official paper / official product site
E4 secondary source (leads only, never proof)

evidence_labels.E1: GitHub REST API record (stars, forks, license, push, release tag)
evidence_labels.E2: Repository source file at default branch (README/manifest/code), self-reported
evidence_labels.E3: Official paper or official product website
evidence_labels.INFERRED: Conclusion drawn by this task from two or more verified observations
evidence_labels.UNVERIFIED: README claim not confirmable in code, manifest, or docs
evidence_labels.NOT_FOUND: No primary source located; no project invented

meta.point_in_time_warning: Stars, forks, push dates and release tags are a 2026-11-05 snapshot and change daily; re-fetch before quoting.
meta.coverage_caveat: bytedance/deer-flow README (380,614 bytes), CHANGELOG.md (1,024,197 bytes) and config.example.yaml (194,493 bytes) were read selectively (headings, architecture, subagents, sandbox, memory, deployment, security, provider sections), not end-to-end. Only quoted/read sections are cited.
meta.readme_marketing_policy: README marketing was not accepted as standalone proof; cross-checked in manifests or source where possible.

cross_references.task-1: Sibling audit reports VPS 2 vCPU / 7.9 GB, no display/GPU, DeerFlow 2.2.0 already deployed at /opt/deer-flow with DEEPSEEK_API_KEY set, and Craft CLIs exposing headless MCP stdio servers. Attributed, not re-verified by task-2.
cross_references.task-3: Craft command/MCP surface audit (not read by this task).

verified_headlines.fact: bytedance/deer-flow is real and current: v2.2.0 released 2026-11-04, backend version 2.3.0-dev, 85028 stars / 11947 forks, MIT, Python >=3.12, last push 2026-11-05. It self-describes as an 'open-source super agent harness'.
FellouAI/eko is real but stale: package/npm version 4.1.3, latest release tag v4.1.0 (2025-12-29), 4960 stars / 446 forks, MIT, TypeScript, last commit 2026-03-03.

Eko ships pauseTask/abortTask, task_snapshot recovery, McpTool, HumanInteractTool, plan/replan agents; its memory is a token-managed message store, not durable long-term memory; README makes no memory or learning claim.
'Harness 2' exists: google-research/harness2 = Harness^2, arXiv:2610.14224, 22790 stars / 2267 forks, Apache-2.0, Python 3.12, created 2026-10-06, last push 2026-11-02.

'superagent' is ambiguous: DeerFlow self-description; deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype (19342 stars, MIT, TypeScript, explicitly 'not an official DeepSeek product', research prototype); plus name collisions forwardemail/superagent (HTTP client) and superagent-ai/superagent (security).

'Hermes' is real: NousResearch/hermes-agent, 260789 stars / 57574 forks, MIT, Python, v0.22.7 (2026-11-03), official site hermes-agent.nousresearch.com, self-improving agent with learning loop and durable memory.

'Hermes hyperagent' exact phrase/project NOT FOUND. Only one 3-star community repo (yurekami/ultragent) mixes HyperAgents + Hermes Agent + Anthropic harness design; the phrase is a conflation of two distinct real things.

'metas hyperagent' exact project NOT FOUND. Closest primary sources: facebookresearch/HyperAgents (Meta, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, arXiv 2603.19461) and stanford-iris-lab/meta-harness-tbench2-artifact ('Meta-Harness', 76.4% Terminal-Bench 2.0, unlicensed).

'hyperagent' maps to at least four things: commercial hosted hyperagent.com (closed source); hyperbrowserai/HyperAgent (AGPL-3.0); facebookresearch/HyperAgents (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); older ICML-2024 HyperAgent bandit algorithm. Never use the term unqualified.

Decisive constraint inferred for this VPS: Craft CLIs expose headless MCP stdio servers and there is no display/GPU (per sibling task-1), so browser/GUI computer-use agents cannot be the execution base; DeerFlow is already deployed at 2.2.0 with DeepSeek configured.

projects.what_it_is: Open-source long-horizon 'SuperAgent harness' that researches, codes, and creates with sandboxes, memories, tools, skills, subagents and a message gateway; 2.0 is a ground-up rewrite built on LangGraph and LangChain.
projects.last_commit_message: fix(mcp): degrade a blob without mimeType instead of failing the tool call (#7800)
projects.runtime: Python >=3.12, FastAPI gateway, LangGraph + LangChain, Node 22+, nginx on port 2026, Docker Compose v2.24+
architecture: LangGraph graph runtime with thread checkpoints and interrupt_before/interrupt_after
Gateway service owning runs, durable threads, cancellation and rollback
Embedded Python client speaking LangGraph SSE protocol
Native task/batch_task subagents with isolated or snapshot context
Pluggable sandbox providers (AIO sandbox, provisioner/Kubernetes mode)
MCP servers (HTTP/SSE + stdio, OAuth, durable background tasks)
Message gateway/channels: Telegram, Slack, Feishu/Lark, WeChat iLink, WeCom, DingTalk
Scheduled tasks (cron), TUI, PATs, token-usage dashboard, monocle traces
projects.tool_interface: Web UI, TUI, HTTP API/Gateway, embedded Python client, MCP client (consumes MCP servers), skills; no official CLI-only mode for crafting
projects.deployment: Docker Compose (make docker-init/start/logs), make dev, make up; binds 127.0.0.1 by default (BIND_HOST to expose); first-run /setup admin; sizing recommendation 8-16 vCPU for a long-running server
projects.memory: DeerMem: user-global summaries in memory.json, Markdown facts per agent under agents/{agent_name}/facts/, deterministic scope/durability/authority write gate, SQLite FTS5/BM25 retrieval under .retrieval/, middleware vs tool modes, optional mem0 / OpenViking-style backends
projects.learning_training: No weight training; learning-by-memory (facts/summaries) and skills. No promotion loop verified.
projects.eval: Per-run monocle traces, token dashboard, sandbox benchmark scripts; no task-quality eval or promotion gate
projects.human_approval: LangGraph interrupts/checkpoints/resume and rollback; no first-class approval queue documented (UNVERIFIED)
projects.deepseek_support: Explicit: deerflow.models.patched_deepseek:PatchedChatDeepSeek; DeepSeek V4 (Thinking) example with supports_vision: false; recommended models list includes DeepSeek v3.2
projects.security_posture: Designed for local trusted environment (127.0.0.1); 'Gateway admin is equivalent to code execution'; rejects client-supplied system/developer messages; IP allowlist/reverse-proxy auth recommended for exposure
strengths: Most complete self-hostable harness among candidates
Native subagents incl. durable batches and context snapshots
Durable memory with deterministic write gates
Skills + pluggable sandbox + MCP both ways
Multi-channel gateway, cron, TUI, Python client
Already deployed on the target VPS at 2.2.0 (task-1)
limits: Heavy for 2 vCPU / 8 GB host (README recommends 8-16 vCPU for servers)
Loopback-trusted by design; exposure requires hardening
Token persistence depends on provider usage metadata
No built-in task-quality evaluation or promotion

recommendation.decision: Integrate DeerFlow 2.2.x as the agent runtime; build the Craft control plane (verification, episode ledger, skill promotion, cost/approval) around it. Do not build a new orchestration engine; do not adopt a GUI/browser agent as the base.
rationale: DeerFlow is MIT, Python-native, actively developed, and already deployed on the target VPS (task-1).
It already provides LangGraph runtime/checkpoints, durable subagents, DeerMem, sandbox, and MCP both ways — the hardest primitives to rebuild.
Craft CLIs expose headless MCP stdio servers (task-1), matching DeerFlow's extension mechanism.
No candidate has Craft-specific verification, eval/promotion, or an episode ledger; those are the build surface and the product's defensibility.

candidate_questions.question: When you wrote 'Harness 2', did you mean Google's google-research/harness2 (Harness^2, arXiv 2610.14224), or the second version of our own harness?
'metas hyperagent': Meta's facebookresearch/HyperAgents (CC BY-NC-SA), the Stanford 'Meta-Harness' Terminal-Bench artifact, or something else you saw?
'Hermes hyperagent': Hermes Agent (Nous, MIT, 260k stars) or Hyperagent (hyperagent.com, closed) - or the Hermes model family?
'superagent': DeerFlow's category name, DeepSeek's dsh-superagent-prototype, or a different product?
DeerFlow: pin v2.2.0 or track main (2.3.0-dev), and what breaks for us between the two?
DeerFlow: can DeerMem use a Postgres/retrieval backend shared with the pipeline DB, or is Markdown + SQLite FTS5 the only durable path?
Are Craft operations exposed to the agent as MCP tools, CLI commands via a shell tool, or both?
Can the DeerFlow gateway container see /opt/craft/** today, or must Craft MCP run host-side behind the stdio<->HTTP bridge?
What is measured memory headroom after one concurrent DeerFlow run on 2 vCPU / 7.9 GB (swap already used)? Is a second run safe?
What is the artifact-of-record per Craft app (project file? rendered PNG? PDF?) and how do we read it back for verification?
Which destructive Craft operations require human approval, and where does that approval live (DeerFlow interrupt, web panel, CLI prompt)?
What does 'promotion' mean for a Craft skill: eval score threshold, N successful episodes, or human sign-off? Who can promote?
Eko: is there an actively maintained fork or a v5 announcement after 2026-03-03? If not, it is reference-only.
Hermes Agent: is there a first-party production guide for a 2 vCPU / 8 GB VPS with a non-Nous model (DeepSeek API), and what is its measured idle RSS?
License policy: are AGPL (HyperAgent) and CC BY-NC-SA (Meta HyperAgents) acceptable anywhere in our stack, even as dev-time tooling?
